$comment: THE TWIN REGISTER — every capability whose logic has been COLLAPSED into an
@ai-matrx/* package. A local definition of one of these names in this repo is a
re-grown twin: the exact failure the client-package campaign exists to kill
(Arman: 'the logic of the packages is NEVER duplicated outside of the package').
Add a row the same session you delete a twin. Never add an allowlist entry to
silence a NEW twin — an allowlist entry is only for a definition that is
PROVABLY not the same capability, and it must say why in `reason`.

A WRAPPER is not a twin: a local function that BINDS the package function's options (unit, style, fallback) and delegates in a line or two is the sanctioned adapter, and needs no entry. A re-implemented BODY is a twin, always.

A SHAPE rule (`shapeWhy` + `shapeAllow` + `shapeCensus` on a row) catches the same capability under an UNREGISTERED name, or with no name at all. `shapeAllow` = provably NOT this capability, silent. `shapeCensus` = pre-existing bodies that ARE it and are not collapsed yet: loud every run, shrink-only, and a stale entry fails the guard.

twins.name: formatFileSize
twins.why: THE byte-size formatter. twins.shapeWhy: A byte count becoming a unit string is this capability whatever it is called. The 2026-09-07 census predicted this gap ('the census method needs a shape pass') and the 2026-09-11 re-verification proved it: formatBytes, fmtBytes, humanSize, bytesHuman, formatSize, and ~60 bare inline JSX expressions that are not definitions at all and can never be caught by a name. Both are covered now. Pattern and its proof: scripts/byte-size-shape.mjs. A capacity constant can never match: the division arms require a DIVISION or THRESHOLD COMPARISON against a byte base, and the multiply arm requires BOTH a non-literal operand (so 80 * 1024 * 1024 is out) AND the unit label on the same line outside any comment (so `limitMb * 1024 * 1024; // 25 MB` is out). shapeAllow.reason: PROVABLY NOT A BYTE COUNT. `compactNumber` renders TOKEN counts for the spend explorer — "1.2M" tokens, "340k" tokens, "812" — and no byte value of any kind enters this module. This is a COUNT formatter and belongs in @ai-matrx/kit/format's forthcoming `formatCount` — it is a future collapse target under that name, not a permanent exemption from byte-size.

NOT a display formatter: gbToBytes/bytesToGb convert between a storage-quota NUMBER and the bare number an admin types into a GB form field (BINARY GB, 1024³, the same base formatFileSize uses — the JSDoc said "decimal" against a 1024³ body until 2026-09-12). There is no unit label and no rounding decision — the string is parsed back into a number on submit, so kit's '1.5 GB' would break the field. The same file's display door on line 27 IS the package (export const formatBytes = formatFileSize).
shapeAllow.why: bytesToGb/gbToBytes are FORM round-trip converters, not formatters: they turn a byte column into the bare number a GB input field edits and back again. There is no unit label and no rendered string — formatFileSize returns "2.0 GB", which cannot go in a number input.

shapeAllow.reason: NOT a display formatter: memoryGrowthMB is a NUMBER written into a machine-readable profiler report whose unit lives in the COLUMN NAME (MemoryGrowthMB), consumed by console.table and by whoever reads the dump - there is no unit label and no human rounding decision. It is also signed: memory that SHRANK is a negative growth, and formatFileSize deliberately returns an em-dash for a negative size.
shapeAllow.why: memoryGrowthMB is a diagnostic REPORT FIELD whose unit lives in the key name (MemoryGrowthMB), pinned to MB on purpose so two runs are comparable. It is a number in a console table, never a unit string on a screen.

shapeAllow.reason: NOT bytes: fmtCount is the research UI's compact COUNT abbreviator — the 'B' it prints is BILLION, beside 'M' for million and 'k' for thousand (1234 -> '1.2k', 6234393 -> '6.2M'). It became visible the day the byte rule learned the decimal family (2026-09-11) and is the one true collision between the two: the letter B means different things in the two vocabularies. formatFileSize would render '6.0 MB' for six million sources.

twins.name: base64ByteLength
twins.why: THE decoded byte length of base64 text (kit 0.13.5, 2026-09-12). There is exactly ONE honest way to compute it and five live sites had written it five ways: `b64.length * 3 / 4` OVERSTATES every padded payload by one or two bytes, because four base64 characters carry three bytes and a trailing `=` / `==` is exactly the bytes that were never there. A sixth adversarial review fixed three sites by hand; a seventh found a FOURTH still wrong (matrx-extend tools/handlers/read.ts, feeding size_bytes) and two of the repairs living as private copies under this same name in aidream's dashboard and in matrx-local. A capability re-derived from memory at every call site is a package export nobody had written yet. The number it returns is real BYTES, which is what formatFileSize wants — the input lane exists because a base64 STRING LENGTH reaching that formatter prints a confident, wrong " KB". NOTE 2026-09-12: the module landed in this repo for kit 0.13.5 but is NOT in the published 0.13.5 tarball — that release was cut from a tree that predated it.
